title: serpine1-corneal-marker: reproducible code and result tables for a marker-versus-network-node dissection of corneal inflammation
description:
Analysis code and result tables for a study that separates marker-grade from network-grade evidence in corneal inflammation.

Eight public transcriptome cohorts (GSE275678, GSE294213, GSE241715, GSE58291, GSE204791, GSE89537, GSE326016, GSE319836) are used to ask two questions separately: (1) does a gene track disease activity across independent cohorts and platforms; (2) does removing it from a co-expression network move an epithelial differentiation programme. SERPINE1 replicates a monotonic gradient in two independent human cohorts (1.65 to 8.90 across four lesion grades; log2 fold change +3.06 for bacterial versus control, external AUC 0.988) but its epithelial nuclear effect is 5.9e-4, one 462nd of TMSB4X, and its residual rank after out-degree detrending is 750 of 947. TMSB4X tops the network ranking (residual 0.246) yet carries no discriminative power in the external cohort (AUC 0.488). The conclusion is that a virtual knockout ranks network position, not marker value. Four control analyses were added in 1.0.6: housekeeping-gene and library checks exclude a global shift; effect magnitude tracks expression abundance (Spearman rho = 0.486), so the ranking is re-read as the top of a continuous peak (96.7th percentile within a joint out-degree by expression-decile stratum, only 12% above mt-Co1 and S100a11); self-knockout rows do not exist in the spectrum matrix; and secreted ligands do not differ from transcription factors (n = 75 vs 28, Mann-Whitney P = 0.73).

The bundle contains the day 1-9 analysis scripts (R and Python), the manuscript figure scripts, 130 result tables with a number-to-file manifest, the sample sheets, and four intermediate matrices too large for the GitHub repository (54, 18, 10 and 2.7 MB). Raw GEO matrices are not redistributed; accessions and file layout are documented in docs/ANALYSIS_ORDER.md.

Known limits, stated in the paper and reproduced here: 20 network reconstructions and 20 degree-preserving permutations bracket the rank estimates, but both stay inside the same linearised engine; combination knockouts are additive by construction; and the discovery cohort separates perfectly for 9 of 10 core genes, so those AUCs are upper bounds.
